title: The zero scheme of a nonzero section of an invertible module on an integral scheme is an effective Cartier divisor
statement: Let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] and let $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)$ with $s\neq0$. Let $Z(s)\subseteq X$ be the zero scheme of $s$ [def-pc-zero-scheme], with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_{Z(s)}\subseteq\mathcal O_X$. Then for every nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ on which $\mathcal L|_U$ is free on a generator $e$, writing $s|_U=a\,e$ with $a\in A$, the element $a$ is nonzero, hence a nonzerodivisor of the domain $A$, and $\mathcal I_{Z(s)}|_U$ is generated by $a$. In particular $\mathcal I_{Z(s)}$ is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], i.e. $Z(s)$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X$ in the sense of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle].

proof.text: Convert module invertibility to sheaf-level invertibility. The section morphism phi is nonzero since evaluating phi on 1 over X recovers s. Apply the proved source Hom.isLocallyPrincipal_zeroLocus underlying lem-pc-zero-scheme-locally-principal, with these explicit sheaf-level instances (not the still-open module-level wrapper recorded by that node). Its zero-locus ideal is nonzero, since a zero ideal would force phi = 0.
The nonzero locally principal zero-locus ideal is invertible on the integral scheme by the closed source ideal-sheaf theorem.

For any chosen affine trivialization, coeff_smul and homOfGlobalSection_app_one identify the ideal with the span of the coefficient. Invertibility makes this affine generator a nonzerodivisor; the domain on a nonempty open is nontrivial, so the coefficient is nonzero. Pair these local assertions with the invertibility already proved.
